questions.q: What does a Record Producer create when a requester submits it, that a standard catalog item does not?
options: An sc_request and sc_req_item, exactly like a standard catalog item
A record directly on a target table of the administrator's choosing, with no sc_request or sc_req_item generated at all
questions.explain: A Record Producer breaks from the standard Request/Requested Item path entirely and writes a record straight onto the target table.

questions.q: In the "Report an Outage" example, what is the target table the Record Producer is configured to write to?
questions.explain: The Record Producer maps its variables directly onto Incident fields, creating a real Incident record on submission.

questions.q: Where is a Record Producer catalog item actually stored?
questions.explain: sc_cat_item_producer is the table that stores Record Producer catalog items, distinct from the sc_cat_item used by standard items.

questions.q: What is the real deciding question for choosing a Record Producer over a standard catalog item, per this lesson?
options: Whether the request needs the standard request-fulfillment lifecycle, or needs to become a record on a different table entirely with no fulfillment-task value from that layer
Whether the catalog item has a Price field
Whether the request form has more than three variables
Whether the catalog item belongs to a subcategory
questions.explain: A Record Producer fits when the standard Request/Requested Item structure would add no fulfillment value; a standard catalog item fits when that lifecycle's tracking and approvals are actually needed.

questions.q: Why would building a Record Producer for a request that genuinely needs manager approval and a fulfillment task be a mistake?
options: Record Producers can only target the incident table
It would throw away the approval-chain and fulfillment-task tracking that a standard catalog item's Request/Requested Item lifecycle provides for free
It is not actually a mistake in any case
questions.explain: A Record Producer bypasses the Request/Requested Item layer entirely, so a process that genuinely needs that lifecycle's approvals and task tracking loses it.
